_comment: One change classifier, shared: scripts/ci/piece_swap.py (hot swap out; .github/piece-swap.json names the classes it acts on), the cmuxterm-hq fix-forward cost model, and the two-commit check read it. A file's class is the first class below whose paths match it (fnmatch, where * also crosses /, and DIR/** is everything under DIR); a file no class matches is `other` (swap never). `swap` says how a piece of the class comes out of a running build without reverting its whole commit: file (a file revert, nothing ships), live (scripts/cmux-next/live_apply.py's web-live or daemon layer: cmux customize, cmux app try, hot-apply), build (out only with a new app build), never (no piece-level neutralizing: its owner's whole revert). piece_roots are the feature boundaries a commit splits on: a root is a path prefix whose * stands for one folder name; every changed file under the same matched prefix (the first root that matches) is one piece, and a file under no root is a piece of its own.

classes.name: drill
classes.why: The post-merge drill's markers: red exactly when planted. Never present on feat-cmux-next.

classes.name: signing-release
classes.why: What signs, notarizes or publishes a build: a half-signed artifact is worse than either whole one.

classes.name: migrations
classes.why: A migration that ran cannot be swapped out; its undo is a new forward migration.

classes.name: published-builds
classes.why: Manifests, pins and resources a published app or package is built from: out only with a new build.

classes.name: web-ui
classes.why: The app's web bundles: a piece swaps out of a running app as a web layer (cmux customize use dir:, cmux app try).

classes.name: rust-core
classes.why: The daemons and linked Rust: a daemon piece swaps by a daemon handoff (hot-apply), an app-FFI piece warm (a relaunch).

classes.name: tools
classes.why: CI, scripts and tests: nothing ships in the app, a piece is a file revert.

classes.name: docs
classes.why: Prose: nothing ships, a piece is a file revert.
